title: Pair-programming SDKs — remote sandbox mentor quickplan (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a short, pragmatic runbook for running 45–90 minute remote pair-programming sessions where a mentor from Developer Experience helps an external integrator (or internal PM/engineer) get an initial SDK integration working against the Redwood sandbox. Focus: unblock first request-to-first-meaningful-output, instrument minimal telemetry, and leave the customer with a reproducible short recipe.

Why this exists (problem statements):
- Many first-time SDK adopters get stuck on environment, auth, or small network edge-cases (CORS, proxies, corporate VPNs).
- Sessions today are ad-hoc and inconsistent: different mentors take different approaches, leading to uneven outcomes and missing telemetry.
- We want a repeatable template that captures quick wins, collects signals, and leaves a clear follow-up path (GH issue, ticket, sample app).

Session types and target outcomes:
- Quickstart (30–45m): goal = one working text generation request + basic token cost estimate.
- Deep pair (60–90m): goal = integrate SDK into a small app flow (chat UI or doc summarizer), enable retries, and capture at least three telemetry signals.

Pre-session checklist (mentor):
- Confirm attendee roles and environment (browser vs server, OS, firewall).
- Send a minimal pre-req note with exact node/python versions, basic env var names, and a short test curl sample.
- Create a disposable sandbox API key tied to the session and a short expiration window.
- Open a GH gist or ephemeral repo with starter code for the chosen language.

Pre-session message template (cut/paste to customer):
"Hey — excited to pair. Quick prep: please have Node 18+ (or Python 3.11+), and an editor open. I will send a temporary sandbox key at start. If you're behind a corp VPN, try running a quick: curl https://api.sandbox.redwood.ai/health — you should see 200. We'll do a 30m/60m run depending on your goal. I'll record notes and follow-ups"

Runbook flow (recommended order):
1) 0–5m: intro + clarifying what they want to achieve this session. Set expectations.
2) 5–10m: environment smoke test — run health curl, check node/python version, confirm network connectivity. If failure, run quick recovery checklist below.
3) 10–25m: first request end-to-end — paste starter sample, swap in session key, get response.
4) 25–40m: basic error handling & retries, show where quotas/errors surface in Console.
5) 40–60m (if deep): wire a tiny UI/handler loop (chat box or file upload → summarizer).
6) final 5–10m: debrief, capture follow-ups, create issue/PR linking sample code and session notes.

Common rapid-recovery steps (if curl or SDK call fails):
- Check API key present and not blank (env var mismatches are the most common).
- Confirm endpoint URL — sandbox vs prod confusion.
- If TLS error, ask them to run: openssl s_client -connect api.sandbox.redwood.ai:443 and paste first few lines.
- For CORS failures on browser demo: fall back to a tiny local server (python -m http.server) or use the node proxy example in the starter gist.
- If corporate proxy blocks, try a simple: curl -x <proxy> https://api.sandbox.redwood.ai/health to validate proxy path.

Minimal telemetry to enable during session (why we collect):
- request.start_ts (to measure cold start for language model variant)
- model.name and model.variant (know which model they hit)
- response.total_tokens and prompt_tokens (quick cost estimate)
- http.response_code and error.type (debug & classification)
Goal: collect at least three of the above for a single happy-path request. Mentor should point out what each metric tells us.

Sample quick commands (copyable):
- Health check (curl):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer SESION_KEY" https://api.sandbox.redwood.ai/health

- Node (minimal):
  import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, baseUrl: 'https://api.sandbox.redwood.ai' });
  const r = await client.text.generate({ model: 'redwood-2-small', prompt: 'Hello' });

- Python (minimal):
  from redwood import Client
  c = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('RW_KEY'), base_url='https://api.sandbox.redwood.ai')
  out = c.text.generate(model='redwood-2-small', prompt='Summarize: ...')

Anti-patterns to call out (common mistakes):
- Running prod keys in a shared REPL or screen-share.
- Trying to batch-block all prompts into one huge call to avoid token costs — explain tradeoffs.
- Assuming default timeout is infinite — emphasize client.timeout and server-side SLOs.

Notes on telemetry privacy and keys:
- Use session-scoped keys whenever possible. Do not keep keys in screenshots or paste history.
- If customer needs logs retained longer than defaults, capture this as an action item and route to support/enterprise-ops.

Post-session artifacts (mentor responsibilities):
- Create a GH gist / ephemeral repo containing any changed starter code and clearly mark lines altered during pairing.
- Open a short ticket (DX-xxxx) summarizing: attendee, outcome, three telemetry samples, follow-ups, and whether a handoff to Solutions Eng is needed.
- Add a short debrief message to the customer with next steps and a disposable replay key (if required).

Measurements and acceptance criteria for the pairing program (how we know it helps):
- Session-to-success ratio: percent of sessions where first request succeeded within 30m. Target: 85% for Quickstart, 70% for Deep pair.
- Time to first meaningful output (median). Target: <15m for Quickstart.
- Follow-up conversion: percent of sessions that led to a sample app PR or paid trial expansion. Target: 20% within 30 days.

Template follow-up message (send after session):
"Thanks for pairing today — great progress. Summary: we got a happy-path text generation working (model redwood-2-small), captured telemetry sample ids: [id1, id2], and wired a tiny chat stub in starter-gist <link>. Next steps: (1) add retry logic per our sample, (2) switch to long-lived key stored in KMS for staging, (3) create PR with app integration. I created ticket DX-#### for follow-up. Ping me if you want a replay session"

Escalation and handoff matrix:
- SDK bug (client crash/serialization): escalate to eng-developer-experience, create linked GH issue and tag @sdk-owner.
- Runtime service error (500/unknown): create SRE incident with logs captured; include session id and approximate timestamp.
- Enterprise or compliance questions: loop in Solutions Eng + security-compliance.

Quick templates and checklists (mentor cheatsheet):
- Before session: sandbox key ready, starter gist link, session note doc created.
- During: capture 1 happy request, 1 failed request (to show error shape), note network anomalies.
- After: gist + ticket + follow-up message + optional replay key.

Open questions / next iteration ideas (to discuss with DX team):
- Should we automate sandbox key creation and revocation into a small web UI templated per session?
- Can we provide a one-click browser demo that eliminates CORS altogether for non-sensitive demos?
- Instrument a lightweight session telemetry tracker (small form) that mentors fill with quick yes/no boxes to capture session signals faster.

Appendix — quick glossary for new mentors:
- sandbox key: short-lived API key we provide for demoing without touching production quotas.
- happy-path: request → valid 200 → structured output that matches prompt intent.
- cold start: first request to a model variant that may incur additional latency.
- telemetry sample id: unique id logged with each request we can use to fetch trace/console entries.

End of doc.
